201	When a due save has waited `AUTOSAVE_MAX_DEFER_TICKS` and only **soft** conditions are closed, it is written anyway and its header is tagged `RISKY`, with `risky_cause` listing every soft input that was true *(Amended 2026-10-27 — user rulings)*. A hard condition is never overridden: a `DOWNED` or `DEAD` world is never written by an autosave or by a Save & Quit (SL-6), and the refractory is never shortened by the cap. *(Orchestrator ruling: R4 says the cap "writes anyway"; read literally that would record the very trap the gate exists to avoid, and would write a state the death stub is about to discard. Three specialists proposed three splits; the ruling is that DOWNED and DEAD are hard, the cap overrides soft conditions only, and the derived loss ceiling in Formulas holds. `GATE_SOFT_STATES` is a systems-designer refinement: a restore drops channel progress and turns `STAGGERED` into `IDLE` (PC-17), and a mid-transit state is Web Map's to restore.)* **Consequence stated plainly:** in the solo MVP a downed seat dies after `DOWN_TO_DEATH_TICKS` 1 800 (or sooner on a `give_up`), well before the cap, so a `RISKY` generation is reachable through chained Graph warning windows held past the cap, a `CRITICAL` suit or an open self-inflicted breach held past the cap, the Attention view, or a transit/channel state held past the cap or at a Save & Quit (SL-6); none of them involves a downed seat. The step-back of SL-8 is no longer near-dead code *(Amended 2026-10-27 — user rulings)*: its fairness route fires on a non-`RISKY` generation, so it runs on every death that follows the restore of an `AUTO` or `EVENT` generation (or a `QUIT` with `VITALS` in its `risky_cause`) within `W_MIN_WARNING_S × TICK_RATE` ticks *(Amended 2026-10-28 — delegated ruling R15)*. The gate also exists to avoid a fairness regression the save would otherwise cause: a generation captured mid-tell restores with only the remainder of the warning (the Graph persists `warn_since_step`, so the elapsed part is kept and the player wakes into a fault with less than `W_MIN_WARNING_S` of it left to perceive), so the Graph's guarantee (`W_MIN_WARNING_S`, endogenous transitions only) would be silently shortened by the save system and a death-stub restore would put the player into a fault with a shortened warning. *(Amended 2026-10-26 — CD-GDD-ALIGN)* **The Graph half (a) prevents this at the MVP.** It is built from the designed Graph read view, not from the undesigned Attention system: `failures()` publishes `cause`, `sev` and `warn_elapsed` per descriptor, and `W_MIN_STEPS` (= `W_MIN_WARNING_S × TICK_RATE / GRAPH_STEP_TICKS`, the Graph's, cited and never restated) says when its gate opens, so a due save waits at most one window (at most `W_MIN_WARNING_S × TICK_RATE` ticks, 600 at the defaults) per descriptor. The Attention half (b) reads the designed `attention.view` but stays optional: without the Attention view the gate is Graph + controller + kernel conditions and logs `GATE_INPUT_ABSENT` once per process. `gate_tell_mode` governs half (b) only; for half (a) FAIR and STRICT collapse into one behaviour (defer for the whole open window), because the window *is* the guarantee. Windows may chain (one closes as another opens); the cap bounds the chain, so `AUTOSAVE_MAX_DEFER_TICKS` and `loss_ticks` are unchanged. **Dormant sections:** a dormant section freezes its `warn_since_step` values in place (Graph dormant-section rule), so a frozen mid-window descriptor never closes; LS-19 names no loaded-section predicate, so the filter "loaded descriptors only" is a routed one-line request to the Graph owner (OQ-38). Until it is answered, a frozen dormant window can defer a save to the cap and tag it `RISKY`, an accepted rare exposure (it needs a derelict unloaded within one window of a new tell). The gate is Formula `autosave_gate` (Formulas); its inputs are injectable for tests. *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review)* *(Amended 2026-10-27 — user rulings)* **What the gate sees, and what it still does not (Resolved 2026-10-27 — user ruling (design-review decisions): OQ-40 and OQ-41 (b), the recommended package adopted).** The gate defers what the world has *already warned about*, and since the ruling it also covers the three cases the review found it blind to. (1) **A suit already critical before any `DOWNED`** is a third soft input, `vitals_block` (row (c); capped, then `RISKY`, no glyph; it also enters `quit_risky`). (2) **A recovery onto a still-critical seat:** after any `DOWNED` → non-`DOWNED` transition no autosave fires for `W_MIN_WARNING_S × TICK_RATE` ticks (the refractory, a hard-type block that expires on its own and that the cap does not override; 600 ticks at the defaults). (3) **A doom with no Graph or Attention tell** (hostile contact, a breach, lethal friendly fire) is not deferred, but it can no longer be restored into unfairly: if the fall follows the restore by fewer than `W_MIN_WARNING_S × TICK_RATE` ticks the stub steps back past that generation whether or not it is `RISKY` (SL-8, the fairness route), unless it is a `QUIT` generation without `VITALS` in its `risky_cause` *(Amended 2026-10-28 — delegated ruling R15)*. A self-inflicted RAGGED breach is the fourth soft input (row (d), OQ-41 (b)). **Still not covered, stated plainly:** a doom that leaves the player more than 600 ticks of acting time after the restore is the world's, not the save's; a STRAINED-yet-doomed seat (31 s of reserve and a 40 s exit) is caught by the step-back and not by the gate (Suit SE-33); and Assembly's optional `pending_any()` soft gate for the one-tick pending window (OQ-41 (a)) was not ruled and stays covered by the `REBASE_BLOCKS` interim (SL-12). The earlier idea of accepting the exposure because the `RISKY` step-back bounds it stays withdrawn, because a doomed save is by definition not `RISKY`.
202	
203	**SL-6 — Save & Quit.** From the pause panel: `request_snapshot` while `PAUSED` (`PAUSED → SAVING → PAUSED`, `T` unchanged), write a generation of kind `QUIT`, and `request_shutdown` only after the write verifies (`WRITTEN`). The call is host-local (CR-15) and is never named a command in the MVP. Quitting is **never deferred** and bypasses the **soft** gate conditions only: if a soft condition was closed at request time the generation is written immediately and tagged `RISKY` (alternatives rejected: refusing to quit traps the player; quitting without writing silently throws away up to one interval). It does **not** bypass the seat-state hard condition: **a `QUIT` requested while any bound seat is `DOWNED` or `DEAD` writes nothing.** `save_and_quit` returns `SL_QUIT_NO_WRITE_DOWNED`, `save_status` is unchanged, and shutdown proceeds after the hold-to-confirm "quit without saving" (art bible HR-14; the look is the Chart Table's); Continue then restores the newest verified generation, which is exactly what the death stub would have done within `DOWN_TO_DEATH_TICKS`. The invariant this buys — **no file on disk ever holds a `DOWNED` or `DEAD` seat** — is testable (Acceptance Criteria). A `QUIT` while a seat is `DEAD` is unreachable in the solo MVP (the stub fires on the `DEAD` tick); the `DEAD` clause is for multi-seat futures. *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review)* **QUIT-then-Continue exposure (resolved, user ruling X7)** *(Amended 2026-10-27 — user rulings)*. A `QUIT` has the same blind spots as an autosave (SL-5). A `QUIT` made with a critical suit is `RISKY` with `risky_cause` containing `VITALS` (the vitals input is in `quit_risky`), so Continue followed by a death inside `DEATH_LOOP_WINDOW_TICKS` steps back past it (SL-8); a `QUIT` made a tick before `DOWNED`, or with no tell at all, is covered by the fairness route (a fall within `W_MIN_WARNING_S × TICK_RATE` of Continue steps back past an `AUTO` or `EVENT` generation; *(Amended 2026-10-27 — re-review, delegated ruling G2, confirmed by R15)* a deliberate `QUIT` generation without `VITALS` in its `risky_cause` is exempt, because the player chose that moment and a step-back would discard a deliberate save and the session before it; a residual exposure, confirmed 2026-10-28 by delegated ruling R15, OQ-52 closed). The post-`DOWNED` refractory does not bind a `QUIT`: a deliberate quit is never refused for it (the seat-state hard condition is the only one that refuses), and a `QUIT` inside the refractory is written at once, tagged `RISKY` only through the soft inputs (AC-SL-129). **QUIT inside an open Graph window.** A `QUIT` made while a Graph warning window is open is written at once and tagged `RISKY`, so Continue restores a fault with less than `W_MIN_WARNING_S` of its warning left. This is a listed exposure with a metric (M4, Edge Cases), and it is **not** clamped: forcing the quit to wait out the window runs the wrong way, trapping the player at the menu to protect a window they can see on screen. The other hard conditions also apply: the kernel-state condition, and an in-flight write (the `QUIT` waits for it), but not the post-`DOWNED` refractory, which binds interval and event saves only *(Amended 2026-10-27 — user rulings)*; in `FAULTED` there is no write path (SL-22). If the write fails, the quit is held, `save_status` reads `FAILED`, and the player may retry or quit without saving by hold-to-confirm. The write waits at most `SAVE_QUIT_TIMEOUT_MS` (measured on the monotonic millisecond source, which is an I/O timeout only, SL-23; polled each frame, never a blocking join, SL-10); on timeout the pause panel stays and `save_status` reads `FAILED`, the job is not abandoned, and one that completes later is simply a `QUIT` generation *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review)*. A window-close request while `RUNNING` calls `save_and_quit()` from `RUNNING` (`RUNNING → SAVING → RUNNING`, K:164) and then `request_shutdown`, under the same rules (it saves the *current* state, so it is no rollback and no oracle); an OS kill (the task manager, power loss) falls back to the newest generation. *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review)* **Close mechanism.** Alt-F4 and the title-bar close are not kills: the OS delivers the same window-close request, so they take the `save_and_quit()` path. The composition root sets `auto_accept_quit = false` so the engine does not exit on the request [UNV: the close notification and this flag are confirmed by the spike]. Save/Load is one Node built by the composition root and owned by it (not an autoload; the worker never touches it); it handles the engine's close notification **without blocking**: it records a `close_pending` intent and polls the writer each frame from `process_mode = ALWAYS` (in `RUNNING`, `PAUSED`, `LOADING` and `SAVING` alike), and `quit()` is called deferred, only after the `QUIT` generation reads `WRITTEN` (or the write was deduped, or the state is a boot-flow screen or `FAULTED`, where nothing is written). **Per state:** `RUNNING` and `PAUSED` run `save_and_quit()`; `LOADING` defers the intent until the kernel is `RUNNING`; `SAVING` lets the in-flight job reach `WRITTEN` or `FAILED`, then dedupes against it (state hash equal, no second write) or writes the `QUIT` generation; any bound seat `DOWNED` writes nothing and holds the close for the hold-to-confirm "quit without saving" exactly as a pause-panel quit does (`SL_QUIT_NO_WRITE_DOWNED`); `FAULTED` and boot-flow screens write nothing. **A failed or timed-out write holds the close; it does not fall through to an exit:** `save_status` reads `FAILED`, the close request is not acted on, and Save/Load publishes the host-local read `quit_held` (bool) so the Chart Table can present its hold-to-confirm (a request to the Chart Table owner, OQ-48). *(Amended 2026-10-27 — consistency pass, ASK-CT-11, EC-CT-38)* A window-close request while `PAUSED` under the open Chart Table (SOLO) runs `save_and_quit()` from `PAUSED` (`PAUSED → SAVING → PAUSED`) under the same rules and then `request_shutdown`; the Chart Table calls nothing and is never a second save path. On a boot-flow screen (main menu, UI-8, UI-9: no SIM state exists and the kernel is neither `RUNNING` nor `PAUSED`) Quit and window close write nothing: the process ends through boot code with no kernel call, because the kernel lists `request_shutdown` only from `RUNNING`, `PAUSED` and `FAULTED` (whether a boot-state shutdown call is wanted is the kernel owner's, ASK-CT-11); from `FAULTED`, Quit keeps `request_shutdown` and writes nothing (SL-22). If the state hash equals the newest generation's (same `T`, nothing changed) the write is skipped and shutdown proceeds. *(Orchestrator ruling: R4/R24 are silent on whether the gate applies to QUIT; three specialists agreed it must not block a deliberate quit, and proposed that it bypass every condition; the stage-5 checkpoint made the seat-state hard condition absolute, because a `DOWNED` generation would have broken the Player Fantasy's promise for up to `DOWN_TO_DEATH_TICKS`. Accepted exposure, from the creative director: Save & Quit before a risky door, quit, relaunch and Continue is a manual save in disguise; the friction of quit-and-relaunch is the only cost (the Zomboid comparison does not carry over, because a Zomboid death is final and a death here restarts from an autosave); determinism means it buys a retry of the player's inputs and, in a deterministic physical world, a look at one visible unknown for at most the minutes since the last autosave (Discovery is aesthetic priority 1, so this is measured, not waved through: triggers M1 to M6 in Edge Cases and AC-SL-94). The interval cannot be the remedy for quit-scumming, because a `QUIT` generation is written at the quit, not on the interval: the response is to accept the exposure for the MVP, keep metric M3 running and escalate to Failure Contract & Re-wake, never deleting the QUIT generation, which would contradict SL-8; OQ-25.)* *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review)*
204	
205	**SL-7 — Death stub (the MVP answer to the Graph's Open Question 1).** "Crew death" in the MVP = every bound seat `DEAD` (single player: PlayerId 1); multi-seat semantics are Failure Contract's and Co-op's. `DEAD` is reached by the `DOWN_TO_DEATH_TICKS` timer or by the solo `give_up` action (user ruling D7), and from `DOWNED` in the pod as well as on foot (statuses run in the pod, user ruling D60); the stub cannot tell the three apart and does not need to *(Amended 2026-10-27 — user rulings)*. Save/Load learns of `DEAD` through the observation channel of SL-13 and, **in the same tick boundary**, settles the writer **without waiting on it** *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review)*: a write job that has already reached `WRITTEN` or `FAILED` is simply a candidate or not, and **a job still busy at the `DEAD` boundary is abandoned** (SL-10, abandon semantics). On the timer path it can only be a hung write: the hard gate has refused every new capture since `DOWNED`, a job started before `DOWNED` has had `DOWN_TO_DEATH_TICKS` (30 s) to settle, and the `DOWNED`-entry command of SL-10 already limited its remaining work to `DEATH_STUB_WRITE_WAIT_MS`. After a solo `give_up` (user ruling D7) it need not be hung: `DEAD` can arrive `GIVE_UP_MIN_TICKS` (the Controller's, 3 ticks = 0.05 s, reached in TAP mode; 48 = 0.8 s is only the default-hold figure, not a floor) *(Amended 2026-10-28 — cross-GDD fix)* after `DOWNED`, long before `DEATH_STUB_WRITE_WAIT_MS` (5 000 ms) can elapse, so a healthy job that was in flight when the seat went down may be abandoned; its generation lands as `STALE_EPOCH` (quarantined, never a candidate) and the stub restores the previous verified generation. That costs at most one more interval, inside the ceilings of F-7, and it keeps a capture taken in the seconds before a fall out of the ring *(Amended 2026-10-27 — user rulings)* Abandonment bumps `write_epoch`, logs `SL_WRITE_ABANDONED_AT_DEATH`, takes the job out of `writer_busy` and leaves the selection to the already-verified candidates; the job's late result can only become `STALE_EPOCH`. There is no join and no blocking wait on the main thread at the `DEAD` tick. Save/Load then bumps `write_epoch` (SL-10), selects a generation (SL-8), and pre-checks and stages it (SL-11), from the hot in-memory copy of the newest verified generation where one exists (SL-11). It then computes the advanced `restore_epoch` (SL-23 (1)), hands its `slot_epoch.bin` write to the worker and polls it once per frame (SL-23 (2), never blocking the main thread). Only after `EPOCH_DURABLE`, or after the write's logged failure or timeout (`SL_EPOCH_NOT_DURABLE`, `save_status = FAILED`), does it call `request_restore(payload, restore_epoch, expected_state_hash)`, which the kernel honours at that boundary's services, normally the first boundary after `DEAD` (the Controller's `DEAD` row and its Edge Case "`DEAD` entered during a camera cut" conform, R14) *(Amended 2026-10-28 — delegated ruling R14)*. Sequence: `DEAD` → (same boundary: in-flight write settled or abandoned, `write_epoch`++, generation chosen by SL-8, pre-checked and staged, advanced `restore_epoch` computed and its `slot_epoch.bin` write issued, SL-23) → (following frames: the epoch write is polled to `EPOCH_DURABLE`, SL-23 (2); the kernel stays `RUNNING` under the `restore_pending` latch with the hard gate closed, and the Presenter holds the down sheet's last frame) → `request_restore(payload, restore_epoch, expected_state_hash)` → kernel `LOADING` (the command queue is flushed, every command `Dropped(RELOAD)`) → the Pipeline shows layer-1 black (`TRANSIT_HOLD`, which the Pipeline lists "kernel `LOADING` entered mid-session (death stub, load)" as an entry condition) → the kernel's restore and the verification window (SL-12) → first `RUNNING` frame is a camera `CUT` at the **pre-load `k_z`**. **No beat, no lights-out, no death screen, no dim-out and no sound** *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review: answers Adaptive Audio's flag F3 — the stub renders no dim-out of any kind, neither sim-driven nor an overlay, and plays no sound; the down sheet's last frame holds, and what sustained cues do at the `LOADING` cut is Audio's own rule, AAV-36)*: the art bible's 2.10 sequence (sources going dark one by one, then the cryo-bay lamp) is written for the cryo re-wake and belongs to Failure Contract & Re-wake (VS-A); the Pipeline's traceability row that says the sequence is "built once in the death stub" is a routed text fix (OQ-14). *(Orchestrator ruling: the brief proposed that the death stub counts as a re-wake for camera purposes and resets zoom to `k_auto`; the locked Pipeline text classes the death stub with in-session loads and says zoom resets "only on re-wake", so the stub **keeps `k_z`**. If Failure Contract wants the reset at VS-A, that is the Pipeline owner's call then.)* `DEAD` during a camera cut is **handled**, not impossible: the stub starts at the tick's boundary and the request is made once the epoch staging step ends (R14), the Presenter holds the down sheet's last frame and no second cut is issued for the death (only `DEAD` during a *cut channel* is impossible, since `DOWNED` precedes `DEAD` by 1 800 ticks on the timer, or by at least `GIVE_UP_MIN_TICKS` after a solo `give_up`, and clears the channel) *(Amended 2026-10-27 — user rulings)*. If no candidate passes the load pipeline, the outcome is `SL_LOAD_NO_LOADABLE_SAVE`: Save/Load publishes `SL_LOAD_NO_LOADABLE_SAVE` and `save_status`; the Chart Table shows it as a boot-flow screen — the kernel is not `RUNNING` and no pause is requested (CT-25) — with New campaign or Quit (the message text is UX's; how a running session whose death stub found nothing is torn down to the boot flow is OQ-42, and from that state the player must be able to reach New campaign or Quit, AC-SL-134) *(Amended 2026-10-27 — consistency pass)* *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review)*; the dead world is never autosaved. The stub attaches no penalty beyond the lost interval. **The one plain line** *(Amended 2026-10-27 — user rulings)*: on the first `RUNNING` frame the HUD shows one ship-log line naming the record that was restored (UI-11), through its `FIRST_FRAME_LINE` channel, keyed on `restore_reason = DEATH_STUB` and carrying the restored generation's playtime. Resolved 2026-10-27 — user ruling (design-review decisions): option (b) of OQ-46 (D15, D84). It is a HUD line, not a screen: it has no death wording, no sound and no dim-out, so the art bible's no-death-screen rule (7.4) stands. Failure Contract & Re-wake replaces this rule at VS-A through the same `request_restore` path and PROFILE store (SL-9). *(Superseded 2026-10-27 — design review, withdrawn in the re-review: the earlier ruling that the stub waits for the in-flight write before it bumps the epoch is gone. There is no wait at the `DEAD` boundary: a job that finished by the boundary is a candidate, a job still busy is abandoned (which bumps `write_epoch`), and `restore_epoch` is computed after selection and staging, then made durable before the request, SL-23 (2) *(Amended 2026-10-28 — delegated ruling R14)*.)* *(Amended 2026-10-27 — re-review)*
206	
207	**SL-8 — Generation selection and demotion.** *Default:* restore the **newest** generation that is not demoted and passes the pre-check (SL-11) — the user's rule, "restart from the last autosave", verbatim. Save/Load restores an *older* generation only when (a) the newest fails the pre-check (fall back newest-first, within `LOAD_MAX_ATTEMPTS`; a reproduction mismatch is never a fallback reason, SL-12), or (b) the **last restored** generation `g_r` (set by the death stub and by Continue alike) is the newest non-demoted verified generation (no newer one exists) **and** one of two routes fires, where `T_downed` is the start of the `DOWNED` episode that ended in `DEAD` (observed through the `loco_state` read SL-13 already grants) and a restore returns `T` to `T(g_r)`: the **RISKY-window route** — `g_r` is tagged `RISKY`, is not a `QUIT` generation unless its `risky_cause` contains `VITALS`, and `T_downed − T(g_r) ≤ DEATH_LOOP_WINDOW_TICKS` 3 600 — or the **fairness route** *(Amended 2026-10-27 — user rulings)* (Resolved 2026-10-27 — user ruling (design-review decisions): X7 (b), D14) — `T_downed − T(g_r) < W_MIN_WARNING_S × TICK_RATE` (600 ticks at the defaults), **independent of `RISKY`**, and of the kind except that a `QUIT` generation without `VITALS` in its `risky_cause` is exempt *(Amended 2026-10-27 — re-review, delegated ruling G2, confirmed by R15)* (OQ-52, resolved by R15). The fairness route covers a capture taken one tick before `DOWNED` and a doom from hostile contact, a breach or lethal friendly fire that no tell announced: a generation that would wake the player into a fall they had under `W_MIN_WARNING_S` to perceive is skipped, which is the unfairness the Graph's `W_MIN_WARNING_S` exists to prevent. The window bounds the player's *acting* time: measured at death it would shrink by `DOWN_TO_DEATH_TICKS`, whose owner range is 600–3 600, so at the Controller's upper bound the rule could never fire. The "no newer non-demoted verified generation" precondition is the loop test: if one was written after the restore the gate opened and the player got out, so there is no loop and the default already picks the newer file. In case (b) `g_r` is **demoted** (renamed `gen_k.demoted`, file kept, never read as a candidate) and selection proceeds as the default; demotion is what keeps (b) coherent — without it the next death would pick the same RISKY newest again and the ring would oscillate (the fairness route demotes a non-`RISKY` generation the same way and for the same reason). If nothing non-demoted verifies, a second pass over demoted generations (newest first) runs before `SL_LOAD_NO_LOADABLE_SAVE`; if the only candidate is `g_r` itself (a loop is detected on either route), restore it and log `SL_STEPBACK_NONE_AVAILABLE`. *(Orchestrator ruling: the brief's unconditional "second death within the window steps back two generations" is not adopted — it reinterprets the user's binding rule. "Step back on a repeated death from a non-RISKY save" is the open question flagged for the user (OQ-1), now narrowed: the user ruled the fairness route only (X7 (b)), and the general form stays playtest-gated. Demotion by rename is a systems-designer addition: it extends the file layout, survives the loss of the manifest, and extends R18; a late-landing write from an abandoned timeline is handled separately in SL-10.)* The selection is Formula `generation_select` (Formulas), which takes `T_downed`. *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review)* **Why `QUIT` is excluded from the RISKY-window route unless the cause is `VITALS`:** a `QUIT` generation is `RISKY` only because the player chose to quit with a soft condition closed (SL-6); an unrelated death shortly after Continue must not step back past a deliberate save and discard its minutes. The exclusion is keyed on the stored `risky_cause` header field *(Amended 2026-10-27 — user rulings)*: a `QUIT` made with a critical suit keeps the step-back, a `QUIT` made with a tell, a breach phase or a channel open does not. The fairness route shares the RISKY-window route's `QUIT` exclusion *(Amended 2026-10-27 — re-review, delegated ruling G2, confirmed by R15)*: a fall within `W_MIN_WARNING_S × TICK_RATE` of a restore is the unfair case for an `AUTO` or `EVENT` file, but a `QUIT` generation is a deliberate save and is stepped back past only when `VITALS` is in its `risky_cause`; the earlier "`QUIT` included" reading made a quit, Continue and a fall within 599 ticks discard the deliberate quit-save and the session before it, a loss F-7 never derived (OQ-52). *(Amended 2026-10-27 — re-review)* **Who performs the demotion, and what a kill does.** The demotion applies **in memory at once** (the ring marks `g_r` demoted before `request_restore`, so the selection never re-picks it); the file rename `gen_k.sav` → `gen_k.demoted` is queued to the **worker** as a `DEMOTE` job, serialised with write jobs on the same queue (a write never races a rename in its own ring) and never run on the main thread. *Crash row:* a kill between `request_restore` and the rename leaves `gen_k.sav` un-demoted. That exposure is accepted and recorded instead of guarded by a `.demote_intent` marker: on relaunch Continue restores that generation (it is the newest again), and a death inside the same window demotes it again, so the cost is at most one extra restore of the stretch the player had already stepped back from (AC-SL-146).
208	
209	**SL-9 — PROFILE store (K OQ 13, D5).** A per-campaign `profile.sav` beside the generation files, in the same container (`file_kind = PROFILE`; no `state_hash`; the trailer and per-block hashes still apply). The kernel produces one snapshot; Save/Load **splits it by `persist_scope` at write time**: WORLD blocks to the generation, PROFILE blocks to `profile.sav`. An in-session restore (the death stub, a load of the already-open campaign) passes **only WORLD blocks** to `request_restore`, so PROFILE blocks are never rolled back (CR-18); a cold open (process start, Continue) loads each scope whole from its own file, because partial restore within a scope is unsupported. `profile.sav` is rewritten, by the same atomic procedure (SL-10), when a capture's PROFILE per-block hashes differ from those last written (no subscription needed), on QUIT, and on an owner change notification (mechanism provisional, as SL-13), which triggers a profile-only capture with no new generation; a floor `PROFILE_MIN_WRITE_GAP_TICKS` bounds the write rate. `profile.sav` keeps a permanent `.bak` (Pillar 5 makes it more precious than any one world generation). A new campaign starts with an empty profile; the death stub and the VS re-wake ("new crew, same world") leave PROFILE untouched, so knowledge survives death in memory by construction and the disk file matters across process restarts. **Zero PROFILE blocks ship in the MVP; the mechanism is specified and tested now** with a synthetic PROFILE block (the kernel's acceptance criterion for `PROFILE` blocks is the model). What is kept at re-wake is Failure Contract's policy. `scope` (SHARED / PER_PLAYER) and `persist_scope` (WORLD / PROFILE) are orthogonal axes: `suit.state` and the Sanity blocks `sanity.state` and `sanity.ledger` are `PER_PLAYER` × `WORLD` in the MVP and **roll back with the death stub**; only knowledge, lore and scars are PROFILE, and none ships. The routed thread's wording "PER_PLAYER / PROFILE" conflated the two axes and is corrected here; the Sanity row in the kernel's Interactions table gives the level `persist` but no `persist_scope`; the designed Sanity GDD and the registry now state `persist_scope WORLD` for both Sanity blocks (OQ-21 closed), and the boot assertion still catches any such gap mechanically (SL-15).
210	
211	**SL-10 — Write procedure and write epoch (D9; behaviour only → ADR candidate "atomic write, backup and thread model").** Capture is synchronous inside the kernel's `SAVING` state (the kernel owns capture cost against `SNAPSHOT_BUDGET_MS`, cited; Save/Load adds, on the main thread, only the encoding of the captured plain data and a small hand-off — Formula `write_budget`, bounded by `SAVE_ENCODE_BUDGET_MS` and `WRITE_HANDOFF_MAX_FRACTION`, both logging thresholds); the payload is an immutable byte value handed to a **worker** that never touches the kernel or any block [UNV: worker threads with file access]. The worker writes `gen_k.tmp` (named `gen_<write_epoch>_<k>.tmp`, SL-10 continued), flushes, re-reads and re-hashes it, renames the position's existing file (the oldest generation, if any) to `.bak`, renames `.tmp` into place, verifies again, deletes `.bak` and rewrites `campaign.json` (state table T-4 in States). **Rules:** every `store_*` return is checked (they return `bool` since Godot 4.4 — sourced from the engine reference); any false return, open error, hash mismatch or rename failure leaves every previous generation exactly as it was, reports to diagnostics and to `save_status`, and the next trigger retries with bounded exponential backoff (`AUTOSAVE_FAIL_BACKOFF_MAX_TICKS`; `AUTOSAVE_FAIL_ESCALATE_COUNT` consecutive failures raise the HUD notice). Never overwrite in place; never delete a generation before its successor verified; **never write while the kernel is `FAULTED`**. The design assumes only that a rename of a closed file to an *absent* name is all-or-nothing; atomic replace on Windows, sharing violations from scanners and indexers and OneDrive-redirected folders are [UNV] and are spike items. "Verified" means readable and hash-correct through the operating system's cache — it does not prove the bytes reached the media (whether a flush implies an fsync is [UNV]); the ring and the recovery scan (T-6) are the answer to power loss, not the verify step. **Write epoch (`write_epoch`)** *(Amended 2026-10-27 — re-review, delegated ruling R1)*: this in-memory, per-process counter was called the "session epoch" and is renamed so it cannot be confused with the persisted `restore_epoch` of SL-23; wherever this GDD says "the epoch" in a write context (`gen_<write_epoch>_<k>.tmp`, `STALE_EPOCH`, "epoch bump", "epoch++"), it means `write_epoch`. Every `request_restore` increments `write_epoch`, which each write job carries; a job that observes an advanced `write_epoch` before its first rename aborts and removes its `.tmp`; a job that had already completed its swap lands a verified generation of the abandoned timeline, which is moved to `quarantine/` as `STALE_EPOCH` and is never a candidate (otherwise a later death would restore the ghost of the previous timeline). Recovery on opening a campaign runs the crash-point scan of T-5: any `*.sav`, `*.bak` or `*.tmp` that verifies is accepted and ordered by `generation`; a file that cannot be proven obsolete is never deleted.
212	
213	**SL-10 (continued) — writer thread contract, polling and abandonment** *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review)*. *Hand-off.* The worker receives only the per-block `PackedByteArray`s (immutable, caller-owned, *(Amended 2026-10-27 — re-review)*), file paths and integers (position, generation, `write_epoch`, retry counts): no kernel reference, no block, no Node and no `Callable` that touches the scene tree, and it never calls `call_deferred` into Save/Load or waits on the main thread. It publishes a status record (`state` ∈ the T-4 write states, `write_epoch`, `generation`, `position`, result code) under a `Mutex` [UNV: the status publication pattern is confirmed by the spike]; the main thread only **polls** that record and never joins the worker, because `Thread.wait_to_finish` and `WorkerThreadPool.wait_for_task_completion` take no timeout, so a join at the `DEAD` boundary would hang the frame on a hung write and could deadlock a worker that reports back through `call_deferred` [UNV: confirmed by the spike, AC-SL-90]. *Polling.* A tick-boundary poll in `RUNNING`; a frame poll from the Save/Load Node with `process_mode = PROCESS_MODE_ALWAYS` [UNV: confirmed in `PAUSED` and `LOADING`] in `PAUSED`, `LOADING`, `SAVING` and during the quit wait, where no tick runs and a tick-boundary poll would never fire. *`DOWNED` entry.* When a bound seat enters `DOWNED` with a job in flight, the main thread sets the job's `finish_or_abort` flag in the status record: the worker completes only its required steps, takes no rename retries beyond the first, skips the manifest rewrite (a hint) and aborts at its first failure, removing its `.tmp`; the remaining work must settle within `DEATH_STUB_WRITE_WAIT_MS` of the command, measured on the monotonic millisecond source (an I/O timeout only, SL-23), else the job is abandoned at that moment. *`DEAD`.* A job still busy at the `DEAD` boundary is abandoned with no wait (SL-7). *General deadline.* A job that has not reported `WRITTEN` or `FAILED` within `WRITE_JOB_TIMEOUT_MS` of its hand-off is abandoned in any kernel state, `DOWNED` or not (`SL_WRITE_ABANDONED_TIMEOUT`, `save_status` reads `FAILED`, `fail_n` is incremented and the backoff of F-2 applies), so a worker that hangs during healthy play cannot hold the hard gate until someone dies; `DEATH_STUB_WRITE_WAIT_MS` stays the shorter limit that starts at `DOWNED` entry. *Abandon semantics.* To abandon a job the main thread increments `write_epoch`, logs `SL_WRITE_ABANDONED_AT_DEATH` (or `SL_WRITE_ABANDONED_TIMEOUT` when a deadline expired), takes the job out of `writer_busy` (an abandoned job never counts toward the hard gate, so one hung worker cannot disable every later autosave) and records its ring position as **claimed**: F-9 skips claimed positions until the job reports, and if no unclaimed position other than the newest generation's remains, the write ends `FAILED` with `SL_WRITE_NO_POSITION` and backs off. Temporary names carry `write_epoch` (`gen_<write_epoch>_<n>.tmp`), so an abandoned job's `.tmp` and a later job's can never be the same file. The worker re-reads `write_epoch` from its status record immediately before each ring-touching rename and aborts (removing its `.tmp`) if it is stale; a job that lands a generation despite that (the check-then-rename race, or a worker that resumed after being stuck past the check) reports its old `write_epoch`, and the main thread moves the file to `quarantine/` as `STALE_EPOCH`, never a candidate (SL-3). The worker is never killed. *Owner.* Capture and every `request_*` call stay on the main thread; the single Save/Load Node (SL-6, close mechanism) owns the worker handle and the poll. *(Amended 2026-10-27 — re-review)* **Thread model, reaping, exit, lock.** *Model:* one `Thread` per job (no `WorkerThreadPool`), its handle held on a `RefCounted` `WriteJob` object that also carries the status record, so the thread's lifetime is the job's. *Reaping:* each poll (tick-boundary or frame) calls `wait_to_finish()` on a job whose thread reports `!is_alive()`; a job that is not alive and has published no terminal `WRITTEN` or `FAILED` status is a worker killed by a GDScript error: `SL_WRITE_WORKER_DIED`, `save_status` reads `FAILED`, `fail_n` is incremented, the ring position is released and the `.tmp` is left to T-6, instead of the 30 s `WRITE_JOB_TIMEOUT_MS` hold of the hard gate. *Cap:* at most `MAX_LIVE_ABANDONED_JOBS` (default 2) abandoned workers may be alive at once; at the cap a new write ends `FAILED` with `SL_WRITE_TOO_MANY_ABANDONED` and backs off until one reports. *Exit:* process exit never blocks on a busy or abandoned worker (no `wait_to_finish` on a live thread); a `QUIT` write that is itself busy follows SL-6's timeout, and an abandoned worker still running at exit is left to the OS, its `.tmp` handled by T-6 on the next open. *Single instance:* the campaign directory is opened under an exclusive lock (`campaign.lock`, created with an exclusive open and holding the process id; the mechanism and its behaviour under OneDrive and antivirus are [UNV], spike rows in AC-SL-30 and AC-SL-90); a second process that cannot take it opens the campaign **READ_ONLY**: it writes no generation, runs no T-6 deletion or quarantine move and offers New campaign and Quit only (AC-SL-147), because two processes would collide on `gen_` and `.tmp` names and T-6 would delete the other process's work.
214	
215	**SL-11 — Load pipeline, pre-check and fallback classes.** All pre-check steps run **before the kernel is touched**, so a bad file never produces `FAULTED`. The pre-check is a pure function of `(bytes, registry view, build constants)` — no clock, no file handle — and is unit-testable over in-memory byte arrays. Pipeline: candidates (ring files plus reconciled leftovers, sorted by header `generation` descending, minus demoted and quarantined) → pre-check (table T-5, a closed `SL_PRECHECK_*` reason set) → stage the decoded WORLD blocks (plus PROFILE on a cold open) → `request_restore` (the kernel orders restore by `restore_after`, runs every `restore()` before any `post_restore()`, CR-8) → verification (SL-12) → `LOADING → RUNNING` with `restore_reason` published (SL-21). **Failure classes decide what happens next:** *(Amended 2026-10-27 — re-review)* **Option A for the death stub; hot copy decoded; writer defects.** (1) *Retries.* The `READ_RETRY_*` retries are frame-polled and apply on **Continue only**; the stub makes **one synchronous attempt per candidate** at the `DEAD` boundary (it must finish inside that tick boundary, which a frame-polled retry cannot), so a locked file there falls through to the next candidate or is served from the hot copy; the `DEAD`-tick work is checked against `DEAD_TICK_HITCH_MS` (AC-SL-88), a threshold separate from the black hold, because the work runs on the frozen pre-black frame that Game Feel 2 says reads as a crash. (2) *Hot copy, decoded.* After a generation reaches `WRITTEN` the **worker** decodes and type-walks it and holds **both the newest and the immediately preceding verified generation** as immutable decoded data (the staged WORLD blocks, handed to `request_restore` read-only; an owner's `restore()` copies what it keeps, OQ-53), so a step-back after a fast death (a solo `give_up` as little as `GIVE_UP_MIN_TICKS` = 3 ticks after `DOWNED` *(Amended 2026-10-28 — cross-GDD fix)*) selects the predecessor without a disk read; the `DEAD` tick only selects, stages and issues the epoch write (SL-23 (2)) *(Amended 2026-10-28 — delegated ruling R14)*, and `t_read + t_decode + t_walk` leave the main thread on the hot path (F-8). A decoded copy that is not ready falls through to the disk chain; copies are dropped on a restore and when their generation is demoted or quarantined; the RAM held is two decoded payloads (a few MiB at the MVP slice, measured by the spike). (3) *Writer defects.* A decode or walk failure at load (T-5 step 19) on a file that passed write-time verification (T-4 `VERIFYING`) is a **writer defect**, not corruption: `SL_WRITER_DEFECT` is logged, the file is marked `suspect`, the next candidate is tried, and the ring is never quarantined wholesale.
216	
217	| Class | Examples | Outcome |
218	|---|---|---|
219	| **CORRUPT** (integrity / structure) | bad magic, truncation, trailer or block hash mismatch, malformed header, decode failure, scope or seat mismatch, caps exceeded, mandatory block missing (with a `registry_epoch` equal to ours) | The file is a **quarantine candidate** (moved to `quarantine/`, never deleted); the loader falls back to the next candidate automatically |
220	| **INCOMPATIBLE** (intact, not ours) | `format_version` or layout unknown, `min_reader_version` above ours, `tick_rate` mismatch, unknown non-retired block, unsupported `schema_version`, a mandatory block missing from a file whose `registry_epoch` differs from ours (**INCOMPATIBLE-dev** *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review)*: "made by an incompatible development build", never quarantined) | **The loader stops** and shows "made by an incompatible build"; files stay in place, never quarantined; the campaign directory is **read-only** for the older build (it never writes a generation into a campaign whose newest header has `format_version` above its own). A silent fallback would roll the player back to an older loadable generation and then overwrite newer files |
221	| **MISSING** | no candidate passes | `SL_LOAD_NO_LOADABLE_SAVE` (SL-7 / menu) |
222	
223	*(Orchestrator ruling: this reorders R10 and overrides R12's "a generation that fails restore twice moves to `quarantine/`" in two ways. First, the trailer SHA-256 moves ahead of any JSON parse or version judgement so a flipped bit in `format_version` is reported as corruption (and falls back) rather than as "made by a newer build" (which must not). Second, the quarantine rule applies to the CORRUPT class and to `QUARANTINE_AFTER_FAILURES` repeated owner-reported restore failures; a **reproduction** mismatch (SL-12) is a code defect — the file hashed fine — so it marks the generation `suspect` in the manifest and keeps the file, because quarantining healthy player files for our own bug would hide them.)* Owner-level failures reported during `request_restore` (`<BLOCK>_RESTORE_*`, for example `GRAPH_RESTORE_UNKNOWN_DEF`) put the kernel in `FAULTED` with the previous state not intact; the kernel's only exits are an explicit user restore or new game (kernel state table) *(Amended 2026-10-28 — cross-GDD fix)*, so the loader's automatic fallback is **limited to pre-check failures**, and after `FAULTED` the menu's Continue re-runs the pipeline on the remaining candidates (SL-22). The pre-check makes that path nearly unreachable by catching everything it can first. Unknown block ids on the build's `RETIRED_BLOCKS` list are stripped with a diagnostics note (a removed block does not strand old saves); any other unknown id refuses, so the kernel's `RESTORE_UNKNOWN_BLOCK` is unreachable — reaching it is a Save/Load defect. A missing block is filled by `default_state()` only when its registration declares `added_in_format` greater than the file's `format_version`; otherwise the file is refused. `LOAD_MAX_ATTEMPTS` (= `AUTOSAVE_GENERATIONS`) bounds one load. For the death stub, the pre-check, decode and staging run **at the `DEAD` tick boundary, before the epoch staging step and `request_restore(payload, restore_epoch, expected_state_hash)` (SL-23 (2))** *(Amended 2026-10-28 — delegated ruling R14)* (the pre-check is pure and needs no kernel); their cost lands in the `DEAD` tick, where the Presenter holds the down sheet's last frame, and **not** in `LOADING`, which holds only the kernel's restore and the verification window of SL-12. *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review)* **Primary path: the hot copy.** After a generation reaches `WRITTEN` the main thread keeps, as an immutable byte value, the complete file image the worker assembled and returned (magic, header, payload region and trailer, T-4 `CAPTURING`) *(Amended 2026-10-27 — re-review)* (the newest verified generation only; replaced by the next `WRITTEN`, dropped on a restore, and dropped when its generation is demoted or quarantined); at the `DEAD` tick the pre-check runs on those RAM bytes, so the death stub does no file I/O when the newest verified generation is the selection, and the decode and type walk (`t_decode + t_walk`, F-8) are the only main-thread cost. **Fallback: the disk chain**, used when no hot copy exists (a cold process, a demoted newest, an abandoned job) or the selection is not the hot generation: candidates are read and pre-checked from disk (a few ms for a ~90 KiB file; cold-cache and scanner latency [UNV]) in the `DEAD` tick. **Step-back pre-stage** *(Amended 2026-10-27 — user rulings)*: only the one candidate a step-back would select (SL-8 (b)) is pre-staged, read and pre-checked on the worker at `DOWNED` entry when `g_r` is `RISKY` and the loop precondition can hold, or when `T_downed − T(g_r) < W_MIN_WARNING_S × TICK_RATE` and `g_r` is not a `QUIT` generation without `VITALS` in its `risky_cause` *(Amended 2026-10-28 — delegated ruling R15)* (the fairness route is decidable at `DOWNED` entry, because `T_downed` is then known); after a solo `give_up` the pre-stage may not finish in the few ticks left, and the disk chain in the `DEAD` tick covers it; it is discarded and re-staged on a `DOWNED → IDLE` recovery, because the gate may have opened in between and written a newer generation. The spike measures the cost of both (OQ-23, AC-SL-88).

225	**SL-12 — Verification: file stage, reproduction stage, and the verification window.** Verification has two stages (Formula `save_verification`, Formulas). The **file stage** is always on and runs before the kernel is touched: trailer SHA-256, every `payload_sha256`, structure. The **reproduction stage** proves the restore reproduced the snapshot: after the last `post_restore()` and **before the first `RUNNING` tick**, recompute `state_hash(PERSIST, T)` (D.12, cited, never restated) over the restored WORLD blocks and compare it with the header's `state_hash`. **Validity guard (needs no kernel hook):** the compare counts only if `kernel.clock.T` equals the header `T` at compare time; otherwise `SL_VERIFY_WINDOW_MISSED` is logged and **no verdict is recorded** (a hash taken after a tick has run would differ for the wrong reason). Its mode is **EXACT** unless one of five closed **REBASED causes** holds: (1) a migration ran, (2) a retired block was stripped, (3) `default_state()` filled a missing block, (4) the header's `hash_algo` is unsupported by this build (the compare is skipped with `SL_VERIFY_ALGO_SKIPPED`; the state hash is a bug detector, and refusing on it would make a kernel hash change a save-breaking event, contradicting SL-16), or (5) a member of the Save/Load-owned build constant `REBASE_BLOCKS` is present in the file. In REBASED mode *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review: the baseline is now read back — the next restore of the same generation, with the same key (`generation`, `build_id`, `registry_epoch`, `trailer_sha8`), `trailer_sha8` being the first 8 lowercase hex characters of the trailer SHA-256 *(Amended 2026-10-27 — re-review: a byte-different file with the same generation number is a different baseline)*; the key is stable because no generation file is rewritten after `VERIFYING`: `restore_epoch` lives in the per-slot side file `slot_epoch.bin` (SL-23, delegated ruling R14), so a restore changes neither a generation's bytes nor its trailer, and the second restore of a generation always finds its baseline (`BASELINE_MATCH` or `BASELINE_DIVERGED` are reachable) *(Amended 2026-10-28 — delegated ruling R14)*; compares its recomputed value with the baseline recorded last time and reports `BASELINE_MATCH` or `BASELINE_DIVERGED` (F-4), so a REBASED load is no longer vacuous against a non-deterministic restore; a first restore records, a later one checks, and a manifest rebuilt from headers has no baseline and re-records)* the recomputed value is recorded as the generation's baseline **in `campaign.json` only** (a hint — SL-14 forbids writing back to the file) and `SL_VERIFY_REBASED{cause}` is logged; it is not a failure. In EXACT mode a mismatch is `SL_VERIFY_NOT_REPRODUCED{blocks}` (naming the diverging blocks when the kernel exposes per-block hashes): **release** builds mark the generation `suspect` in `campaign.json` and **play on**; **dev and test** builds halt on the first occurrence (it is a K:839 / G4 regression). A reproduction mismatch **never falls back to another generation**: the file stage has already proved the bytes, so a mismatch after a successful restore is deterministic code (`restore(snapshot) ≠ identity`) that reproduces on every generation, and walking the ring would strand the player on an intact ring with `SL_LOAD_NO_LOADABLE_SAVE` for our own defect. `SUSPECT_THRESHOLD` is a diagnostics escalation only. *(Orchestrator ruling — findings the first rulings did not settle, as amended at the stage-5 checkpoint. (1) R10 says the compare runs after every restore in every build; applied literally, the first schema bump would fail every older generation (a migrated block's canonical bytes differ from the stored ones), hence the EXACT/REBASED modes and their closed cause set. (2) **Restore-idempotence is the kernel's rule, not a Save/Load request:** K:839 already requires, for every registered block, that the snapshot → interchange → restore → snapshot round trip yields byte-identical canonical bytes, and G:1096 is the Graph's instance of it; a registration flag that let a block opt out would be a CR-8 field invented by Save/Load and would make verification permanently vacuous, so none exists. The Controller's restore is a non-identity (PC-17: `octant`, `run` and `channel_ref` reset and `CHANNELLING` / `STAGGERED` become `IDLE`; the Controller draft's Body text zeroed `sub` and set `previous := current` in `post_restore`, P:913, while P:285 persists `sub` — answered for `body.state` by Ship Body & Interior Physics BDY-31: `post_restore` preserves `sub`, and `body.state` is restore-idempotent at block level *(Amended 2026-10-27 — consistency pass)*), and the Controller's G4 claim (P:1045) cannot hold while the control run carries sub-pixel residue that the restored run zeroes and the live Adapter's resync command is absent from a replayed stream. That is routed to the Controller/Body author as a **CONFLICT against K:839 and G4** naming those three specifics — PC-17 restore normalisation; `sub = 0` and `previous := current` in `post_restore` against a persisted `sub`; the P:1045 replay claim against the residue and the absent resync command (OQ-9) — and the resolution is the owners': express the normalisation in `snapshot()` or move it out of restore. **Interim, Save/Load-owned and provisional** *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review: one reading of PC-17 across this rule, SL-15 item 10, OQ-9, OQ-39 and the knob row)*: the build constant `REBASE_BLOCKS` lists the blocks whose presence selects REBASED mode. **Default `[interaction.state, assembly.state]`.** `controller.state` and `body.state` are **not** listed: the Controller answered that PC-17 normalises in `snapshot()` and that `restore()` is a whole-block replace, and BDY-31 makes `body.state` restore-idempotent at block level, so the automated AC-SL-67 (a mid-move `controller.state` fixture compared in EXACT mode) is the gate that proves it, and a story whose fixture fails it re-adds the block with a dated debt entry. `interaction.state` and `assembly.state` still clear transient fields in `post_restore` (IA-36, MSA-4), so a generation saved mid-channel or inside Assembly's pending window would verify `NOT_REPRODUCED` and halt a dev build on a routine quit mid-weld; they are listed **now**, so no merge halts dev builds, and the **exit** is that the owners move the clears into `snapshot()` (OQ-39, routed), after which Save/Load empties the list and the default becomes `[]`. A non-empty list is a known kernel-contract debt: while it holds, every real MVP file contains a listed block and verifies REBASED, which makes the reproduction stage diagnostic-only for real saves (the recorded baseline above still catches a restore that is not deterministic), and a CI check fails the first outside build while the list is non-empty (SL-14). The through-disk G4 criteria run on the kernel's stand-in blocks, `graph.state`, `controller.state` and `body.state`, and AC-SL-67 is a merge gate for the Controller, Interaction and Assembly stories. (3) **K-4 (adopted by the kernel, CR-15)** *(Amended 2026-10-28 — cross-GDD fix)*: `request_restore(payload, restore_epoch, expected_state_hash = none)`. When an expected hash is given the kernel recomputes `state_hash(PERSIST, T)` after the last `post_restore()`, inside `LOADING` and before the first `RUNNING` tick, and reports `{T, computed_hash, match}` to Save/Load, never as a `FAULTED` transition (release plays on). Save/Load passes the header `state_hash` in EXACT mode, the recorded baseline in REBASED mode when one exists, and otherwise the header value with `match` ignored; F-4 takes `recomputed = computed_hash` and `window_ok = (reported T == header.T)`. The harness compare (dev/test) stays as a second path. Restoring into `PAUSED`, verifying and resuming stays rejected (it conflicts with the Pipeline's `LOADING → RUNNING` `CUT`, with single-player-only pause in CR-16 and with VS-B's reuse of the restore path).)* Integrity here is against accidental corruption, not tampering (host-owned saves, no PvP, no leaderboard).

227	*(Amended 2026-10-27 — re-review)* **Per-build verification table.** The build flag is derived from the engine feature tags: `release` = `OS.has_feature("template_release")`; `dev` = any other run (editor or `template_debug`); `test` = `dev` plus the harness flag [UNV: the feature-tag names are confirmed by the spike; the engine reference has no OS module]. The table replaces the three inconsistent descriptions of release behaviour in SL-1, SL-16 and F-4.
228	
229	| Build | Header `state_hash` written at capture | Reproduction compare on load | A file from the other kind of build |
230	|---|---|---|---|
231	| `release` *(Amended 2026-10-28 — cross-GDD fix)* | Written (K-4 adopted, kernel CR-15; SL-1, SL-16) | Runs inside `LOADING` through the kernel's K-4 report under the EXACT / REBASED rules of this paragraph with the same `REBASE_BLOCKS` | A file that carries `state_hash` loads, the compare following the row above; a file from an earlier release build without it loads with verdict `NONE` |
232	| `dev` | Always written | Runs; EXACT mismatch halts, REBASED records and later checks the baseline | A file from an earlier release build (no `state_hash`) gives verdict `NONE`: never CORRUPT, never quarantined, never a halt |
233	| `test` | Always written | Runs as `dev`, with the injectable halt handler | As `dev` |
234	
235	`REBASE_BLOCKS` makes a real MVP save REBASED in every build that compares; that is the stated, temporary diagnostic-only state of this paragraph, not a release-only effect. The outside playtest (AC-SL-94) must run on a `release` export, so testers hit the shipped behaviour.
236	
237	**SL-13 — Observation channel for a control-plane caller (provisional — kernel owner).** Save/Load is a host-local control-plane caller (CR-15), not one of the kernel's five subscriber classes (PRESENTATION, INPUT_SURFACE, PROJECTOR, REPLICATION, DIAGNOSTIC). Its reads are limited to: `kernel.clock` (`T`, `world_seed`); `controller.state.loco_state` per bound seat (its `DOWNED` → non-`DOWNED` transitions give the refractory's `last_recover_T`, SL-5) *(Amended 2026-10-27 — user rulings)*; the Life-Support Graph's `read_view.failures()` for the Graph half of the soft gate (designed, LS-19; required at MVP; a SIM read with no perceived variant, so it is not a `PERCEPTION_OUT` view) and the optional Attention SIM view `attention.view` for the Attention half (designed; absent = open); Suit's `view(player_id).vitals_state` per bound seat for the critical-suit input (designed, SE-33, a SIM read) and Assembly's pure read `ragged_breach_open()` for the open-breach input (registered, source Modular Ship Assembly) *(Amended 2026-10-27 — user rulings, consistency follow-up)*; the event-trigger reads of SL-4 (the `POD_ARRIVED` notification, Assembly's pure read `last_shape_change_T()` and Interaction's pure read `last_salvage_T()`); and the Controller's end-of-tick change notification for `controller.state` (for the death stub) and for any PROFILE block (for SL-9). It **never** reads a `PERCEPTION_OUT` view (CR-12, H5) and **never writes a block** (H3, H4). *(Amended 2026-10-27 — re-review, delegated ruling R1)* It reads no epoch: `restore_epoch` is Save/Load's own persisted value (SL-23) and reaches the sim as an argument of `request_restore`, never as a read. Which subscriber class or read access a persistence service has is not stated by the kernel's interaction table; it is routed to the kernel owner (OQ-7), and until it is answered every observation is a tick-boundary read-view poll made in the same boundary in which the request will be issued.
238	
239	**SL-14 — Versioning and migration (D7).** Two levels. **Container** `format_version` (from 1, `FORMAT_VERSION`) is migrated by Save/Load; **block** `schema_version` is migrated by the *owner* inside `restore(data, stored_version)` as a chain v → v+1 → …, each step a registered pure function `(old dictionary) → new dictionary`. **Save/Load never rewrites a block's data itself** — owners are the only writers of their shape. Save/Load verifies, in the pre-check (T-5 step "schema chain"), that the chain is complete for every stored block (a gap is `SL_PRECHECK_SCHEMA_UNSUPPORTED`, never a mid-restore failure). A migrated payload is **not written back** to the old generation file; the next autosave writes the new shape, so a downgrade followed by an upgrade cannot half-migrate a file. A persisted WORLD block is **mandatory** for a file iff its registration's `added_in_format ≤ file.format_version`; the MVP mandatory set (SL-25) is the *expected result* of that rule, not a hand-kept list. An **additive bump** — a new block added after the first outside build — is `format_version + 1`, `min_reader_version` = the new version, container migration = identity, the new block filled by `default_state()`; defining it keeps the friction of adding a block constant. `added_in_format`, `RETIRED_BLOCKS` and the mandatory flag live in one data file cross-checked against the live registry at boot (→ ADR candidate). **Policy:** the machinery exists from format 1 and two goldens are kept *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review)*: a **stand-in golden** in `tests/fixtures/saves/v1-standin/`, regenerated freely while the registry is still moving (it exercises the machinery, not any shipped shape), and a **frozen golden** in `tests/fixtures/saves/v1/`, generated from the real registry at the first outside build and immutable from then on, with a schema-drift fingerprint check in CI (the committed shapes' `registry_epoch` digest may change only together with a `schema_version` or `format_version` bump) — the Graph's acceptance criterion names the convention; the **obligation** to migrate begins with the first build given to anyone outside the project (the three-person MVP playtest); earlier development saves are disposable and are refused with "made by an incompatible development build" *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review: the signal is the header `registry_epoch` — a file whose epoch differs from ours and fails a mandatory-set or schema step is INCOMPATIBLE-dev and never quarantined, so registering one more block does not turn every dev save into a quarantined CORRUPT file)*. That policy is Save/Load's own; the Graph's citation of a Layout open question ("pre-release saves are disposable") is answered from the Layout side *(Amended 2026-10-27 — consistency pass)*: a renamed `room_key` or `template_id` needs a migration step in the owner once the first build has been given outside the project; before that, saves are disposable (this rule; OQ-12 closed). After the policy begins, a rename of a `def_id` or a `room_id` needs a migration step in its owner. The header's `catalogue_version` (designed — Item & Module Database, IDB-26, IDB-27) lets the owner detect a content-epoch change. A header `catalogue_version` above or below the running catalogue's is never a pre-check refusal (it is not a T-5 step): the load proceeds and each holder's `restore()` decides, with `GRAPH_RESTORE_UNKNOWN_DEF` as the model — this answers the Item DB's OQ 7 and its edge case on a save written under a higher `catalogue_version`. An unknown `def_id` at restore stays the owning block's named failure (`GRAPH_RESTORE_UNKNOWN_DEF`), and a `renamed_from` alias honoured only at restore is the Item DB's to offer. `format_epoch` (the brief's separate field) is **dropped**: `format_version`, `min_reader_version` and `added_in_format` cover it.
240	
241	**SL-15 — Block authoring contract (R23; layered on CR-8, not a kernel amendment).** Save/Load's main deliverable to every block owner. A `persist` block must:
242	
243	1. carry a namespaced `block_id`; declare `class`, `persist`, an explicit `persist_scope` (WORLD or PROFILE) and `scope`; a `PERCEPTION_OUT` block is never `persist`;
244	2. declare `schema_version` ≥ 1, bumped on any serialized-shape change, and `supported_versions` (the kernel's pre-check uses the list only "if owners declare"; Save/Load requires it) containing the current version;
245	3. return from `snapshot()` plain data only (H7: primitives, arrays, dictionaries, packed arrays; no `Vector2i` — integer vectors travel as two ints or a packed int array), in deterministic order, with entity references by stable ID and **no** derived caches, object references, `Resource` or `Node`; untyped containers; no `StringName` keys; an `ItemInstance` inside a snapshot is the Item DB's `to_array()` array, never a Dictionary (SL-2, IDB-15) *(Amended 2026-10-28 — cross-GDD fix)*;
246	4. encode 64-bit data per S-1 (owner values above 2^53 never become float-typed JSON numbers; they travel inside the binary payload);

269	| `SL_BOOT_KNOB_RANGE{knob}` *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review)* | a tick or byte knob lies outside its safe range (OQ-28, decided): checked **before** any invariant, so no invariant ever divides by an out-of-range knob |
270	| `SL_BOOT_KNOB_INVARIANT{id}` | a Tuning Knobs invariant I1–I8 or I10–I13 fails against the data file *(Amended 2026-10-27 — user rulings)*; I9 is a boot refusal in a **release** build and a logged diagnostic in dev and test *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review)* |
271	
272	**SL-16 — Hash roles (D8; R10, R15).** Four distinct integrity layers, no overlap. (1) The **file trailer** SHA-256 over every preceding byte and (2) the per-block **`payload_sha256`** over each stored payload — Save/Load's own, fixed, native [UNV], verified before the kernel is touched; they localise damage and guard accidental corruption and truncation, not tampering. (3) The header **`state_hash`** and the optional per-block **`block_state_hash`** are the *kernel's* 64-bit hash over the owners' canonical bytes (D.12), named by `hash_algo`, so the ratified hash (H64 = first 8 bytes, little-endian, of SHA-256 via `HashingContext`, `hash_algo` 2; R-17, user ruling X13, registry `state_hash`) and the per-block cached hash (**K-1**, a kernel ADR candidate — cited, never owned) can change with no `format_version` bump *(Amended 2026-10-27 — user rulings, consistency follow-up)*; `block_state_hash` is present only if the kernel exposes a per-block hash, is diagnostic and is never a refusal reason. (4) The post-restore **reproduction compare** of SL-12 detects a restore that does not reproduce the snapshot — a bug, not corruption. The kernel's D.11 worked example assumed the hash cost is a debug-build cost; this design makes it a release cost on every capture and restore, and the ratified H64 is native, so the remaining cost question is whether SHA-256 over 100–300 KiB stays near the 1.5 ms that example allowed [UNV] — the spike (AC-SL-89) measures it, and K-1 is the mitigation if it does not (OQ-2, OQ-17) *(Amended 2026-10-27 — user rulings, consistency follow-up)*. *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review)* Godot's `HashingContext` offers only MD5, SHA-1 and SHA-256 [UNV: 4.5 – 4.7 are post-cutoff, confirm in the spike], so a scripted `hash_algo` 0 (xxHash64) or 1 (FNV-1a 64) would be a per-byte loop, estimated at 15 to 150 ms over ~90 KiB (the range between the first review and the game-designer's estimate) [UNV]; a hitch that appears only on writes would tell the player when the game saved, the signal UI-1 was retired for. **Ratified** *(Amended 2026-10-27 — user rulings, consistency follow-up)*: the default is the **native truncated SHA-256** (`hash_algo` 2, H64), which `HashingContext` computes natively (R-17, user ruling X13). With K-4 adopted (kernel CR-15) the capture-time `state_hash` has a release consumer and is written in every build (SL-1) *(Amended 2026-10-28 — cross-GDD fix)*.
273	
274	**SL-17 — Zero blocks, zero hooks (D13).** Save/Load registers no state block and no step hook: ring bookkeeping lives in `campaign.json`, because a WORLD block would roll back on restore and desync the file set from the world. The kernel's acceptance criterion that the registry holds exactly one block, `kernel.clock`, stays true with Save/Load booted. The MVP save request is a host-local API call (CR-15), so CR-16's "save-request state" is not needed. A `saveload.request_save` command type (`origin PLAYER`, `allowed_when_paused`, `actor_binding NONE`) for VS-B guests is **reserved and (provisional — Co-op Session & Replication, VS-B)** at every mention; nothing in the MVP depends on it.
275	
276	**SL-18 — New game entry (D14; routed amendment K-2).** Save/Load owns only `new_game(world_seed)`: create the campaign directory and a random `campaign_id`, write `slot_epoch.bin` = 0 (SL-19, SL-23 (0); a failure is not fatal, because a missing file reads by the SL-23 (2b) recovery rule), call the kernel's `request_new_game(world_seed, restore_epoch = 0)` (kernel CR-15, CR-18), which sets `world_seed` into `kernel.clock`, and write the **initial generation** *(Amended 2026-10-28 — delegated ruling R14; cross-GDD fix)* (kind `EVENT`, trigger `NEW_GAME`) at the first tick boundary after the world is constructed, so a death before the first interval restores a fresh world rather than nothing. *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review)* The world is built by the kernel's `init_world(world_seed)` owner step, which is **adopted** (kernel CR-18, K-2): every owner that registers `init_world(world_seed)` runs it in `LOADING`, in `restore_after` order, under one `WriteScope`, after every `default_state()` and before `post_restore()`, and never on a load from a save. The MVP world build is Web Map & Transit's `init_world` (WM-7), which builds the home-ship, the two hand-made derelicts and the pod through Layout's `build_section`; Save/Load owns none of it and only observes its end, and AC-SL-75 re-checks the ordering against CR-18. World content is Web Map's, Layout's and Authoring's. If world construction fails, or the baseline cannot be written after `AUTOSAVE_FAIL_ESCALATE_COUNT` attempts, the empty campaign directory is removed (it holds no verified generation, so the no-deletion rule is intact) and the menu receives `SL_NEW_GAME_NO_BASELINE`: a campaign with no verified generation would make the first death unrecoverable.
277	
278	**SL-19 — Directory layout, compression, settings (D15–D17).** `user://saves/<campaign_id>/` holds `campaign.json` (the manifest hint), `gen_0.sav … gen_{N−1}.sav`, transient `.tmp`/`.bak`, `slot_epoch.bin` (the slot's live `restore_epoch`, u32 + CRC32, SL-23 (0)) and its transient `slot_epoch.tmp` *(Amended 2026-10-28 — delegated ruling R14)*, `gen_k.demoted` files (SL-8), `profile.sav` and its `.bak`, and `quarantine/` (files moved there carry a reason — `CORRUPT`, `RESTORE_FAILED`, `STALE_EPOCH` — and their **generation number in the file name** (`g<generation>_<REASON>_<k>.sav`; the physical reason encoding stays OQ-27, the generation number is fixed now so `gen_next` can read it without opening the file) *(Amended 2026-10-27 — re-review)* — and are never deleted automatically; the folder's size is reported in diagnostics against `SL_QUARANTINE_SIZE_ALARM_BYTES`, a diagnostics threshold only; deletion happens only through the explicit campaign delete under hold-to-confirm). `campaign_id` is 128-bit random hex; one campaign exists in the MVP, many are permitted (Alpha host-owned worlds). Starting a new campaign over an existing one is destructive and defaults to retiring the old campaign (renaming it out of the active location); deletion is a separate explicit action under hold-to-confirm (HR-14, art bible; the UI is the Chart Table's). **No compression in the MVP** (typical size ≈ 100–300 KiB, kernel D.11 expectation); header `codec` 0 with 1 reserved; a size alarm at `SAVE_SIZE_ALARM_BYTES` 2 MiB (diagnostics only), re-evaluated at VS-A (600–1 200 Graph nodes). **Settings and key bindings are never in a snapshot**: Settings & Input Rebinding (Alpha) owns a per-client `ConfigFile`; Save/Load may expose only the atomic-write helper. Steam Auto-Cloud is Alpha and constrains the path layout only.
279	
280	**SL-20 — Identity (D12).** The header `seats` list names the PlayerIds present, **for validation only**; `PER_PLAYER` blocks are keyed by PlayerId inside their own dictionaries; the binding table (`peer_id → PlayerId`) is never saved (kernel CR-7): the peer half is session state (the session owner binds `HOST_PEER_ID` 1 → PlayerId 1 at boot and a restore never touches it); the `PlayerId → {controlled entity IDs}` half is never saved either and is rebuilt **by the kernel** as the last step of every `LOADING` (kernel CR-7, KRN-BIND-01) from the owners' restored blocks (Body `seat_bindings()`, Emitter `beam_bindings()`). Save/Load adds no step, writes no binding datum, and its death-stub and Continue paths need only `request_restore` (the epoch staging of SL-23 (2) precedes the request; the rebuild runs inside `LOADING`) *(Amended 2026-10-28 — cross-GDD fix)*. Single-player is PlayerId 1 bound to `HOST_PEER_ID` 1. A file whose `PER_PLAYER` keys are not a subset of `seats`, or whose `seats` is empty, duplicated or out of range, is refused (`SL_PRECHECK_SEATS_INVALID`). "Keyed by peer ID" is a stale token; a reconnecting peer with a different transport id changes nothing in a save.
281	
282	**SL-21 — Published reads, `SaveInfo`, `restore_reason` and the host-local API (R7, R20, D11, D18).** Save/Load publishes **host-local reads**, never commands and never blocks: `save_status` ∈ {`IDLE`, `WRITING`, `WRITTEN`, `FAILED`} (`WRITTEN` is sticky until the next write begins and carries `written_at_T`; no HUD element displays it per write, *(Amended 2026-10-26 — CD-GDD-ALIGN)*); `fail_escalated` (bool) *(Amended 2026-10-27 — consistency pass, HUD OQ-HS-21)* — true from the `AUTOSAVE_FAIL_ESCALATE_COUNT`-th consecutive failed write until the next `WRITTEN`, because `save_status` reads `FAILED` on every failed write and the HUD counts nothing (HS-46); `SaveInfo` for the newest generation — campaign id, generation, kind (`AUTO`/`EVENT`/`QUIT`), `T`, playtime (`T div TICK_RATE`, whole seconds, integer floor — OQ-30), `game_version`, crew count, `RISKY`, depth label (provisional — derived from the node `ring` of `web.view`; Web Map publishes no depth-label field) — **computed from SIM blocks at capture** (`RISKY` stays on the read for diagnostics and the Debug Overlay; no player-facing line shows it, user ruling D82 *(Amended 2026-10-27 — user rulings)*); and `restore_reason` ∈ {`NEW_GAME`, `LOAD_GAME`, `DEATH_STUB`, `FAULT_RECOVERY`}, valid for the first `RUNNING` frame after `LOADING`. *(Amended 2026-10-27 — re-review, delegated ruling R1)* Also published, diagnostic only: `restore_epoch` (u32, SL-23); the sim reads the value only through `kernel.clock`. **`restore_reason` is a routed request, not an existing flag:** the Pipeline GDD has no such field (a search finds zero hits), so the brief's statement that the Pipeline was already amended is false; this GDD offers the flag as *provided* and requests it of the Pipeline, HUD & Suit Layer (designed, hud-and-suit-layer.md; the request stands) and Failure Contract & Re-wake (provisional — undesigned); the HUD's UI-11 line is the MVP consumer of `DEATH_STUB` (user ruling D15) *(Amended 2026-10-27 — user rulings)*, and no consumer may use `DEATH_STUB` to alter hallucination content (SL-24). **There is no screenshot thumbnail** (it would capture the Perception Filter's lie, Pillar 1), **no audio cue** (any sound is attributable by the web, Pillar 3, unless Audio justifies one) and **no death screen** (art bible 7.4). 458	### Interactions with Other Systems

460	**What Save/Load exposes and consumes, in names fixed elsewhere.** It registers **no hooks, no mutators, no commands (the VS-B `saveload.request_save` is reserved and provisional), no blocks and no dirty keys** (SL-17), and it never writes a block (H3, H4). It calls the kernel's host-local control plane — `request_snapshot`, `request_restore(payload, restore_epoch, expected_state_hash)`, `request_new_game(world_seed, restore_epoch = 0)`, `request_shutdown` (CR-15, CR-18) *(Amended 2026-10-28 — cross-GDD fix)*; `request_pause` / `request_resume` are the pause panel's, not its own. It reads `kernel.clock`, `controller.state.loco_state` per bound seat, the Graph's `failures()` read view and an optional Attention SIM view (SL-13). It publishes the host-local reads `save_status`, `SaveInfo` and `restore_reason` and the API of SL-21. All three rules for every consumer in the kernel's Interactions section hold: a system that wants state to persist registers a block and never talks to Save/Load directly. **Every interface with an undesigned or in-flight system below is provisional — it lists only what that system must supply or may rely on, never a guess of its internals.**

518	## Formulas
519	
520	All sim-time quantities are **integer ticks** read from `kernel.clock.T` and converted to seconds only in examples, at `TICK_RATE` 60 (registry, cited). Anything hashed or stored in a header is an integer or an exact-width hex string (S-1); a millisecond budget below is a float used only for logging thresholds, is never hashed or replicated, and so is outside the kernel's determinism rule. **Cited, never restated:** `state_hash` (kernel D.12, registry), `rng_derive` (kernel D.10, registry), `snapshot_bytes` and `capture_time_ms` (kernel D.11), `SNAPSHOT_BUDGET_MS` and `MAX_BLOCKS` (kernel GDD values, not registry entries — kernel registry candidates), `DOWN_TO_DEATH_TICKS` (registry, Controller), `W_MIN_WARNING_S` (registry, Graph). Owned constants are named in Tuning Knobs. Ten formulas follow; the first six are the registry candidates of the rulings (R29, with `generation_select` and `save_verification` amended at the stage-5 checkpoint), the last four are derived bounds and encodings the criteria need.
521	
522	### F-1. `autosave_due`
523	
524	The `autosave_due` formula is defined as:
525	
526	`elapsed = T − last_save_T; interval_due = elapsed ≥ AUTOSAVE_INTERVAL_TICKS; event_due = (pending_events ≠ ∅) AND elapsed ≥ AUTOSAVE_MIN_GAP_TICKS AND NOT (ragged_breach_open() AND ASSEMBLY_CUT ∈ kinds(pending_events)); due = interval_due OR event_due; kind = EVENT if event_due else AUTO` *(Amended 2026-10-27 — user rulings)*
527	
528	**Variables:**
529	
530	| Variable | Type | Range | Source | Description |
531	|---|---|---|---|---|
532	| `T` | int | 0 … 2^63 − 1 | `kernel.clock` (read at the tick boundary) | Current sim tick |
533	| `last_save_T` | int | 0 … `T` | Save/Load session memory: the capture `T` of the newest durable generation; reset to the restored generation's `T` on every restore | Basis of the loss window; unchanged by a failed write, so a failed save stays due |
534	| `event_pending` | bool | {0, 1} | Owner notifications and pure reads (SL-4): `POD_ARRIVED` (`web_events`), `last_shape_change_T()` (Assembly), Interaction's `last_salvage_T()` (BS-21) — `POD_ARRIVED` provisional until merge; coalesced; cleared when a capture at or after the event's tick is `WRITTEN` | At least one autosave-worthy event (pod-hop arrival, weld or cut completion, dock, section extraction) since the last write. *(Amended 2026-10-27 — re-review)* `event_pending` is the predicate `pending_events ≠ ∅`, where `pending_events` is a **set of `(kind, tick)` entries**, not one coalesced kind: a later event adds an entry and never overwrites an earlier one, and an entry leaves the set only when a capture at or after its tick is `WRITTEN` |
535	| `event_kind`, `ragged_breach_open()` *(Amended 2026-10-27 — user rulings)* | enum, bool | {`ASSEMBLY_WELD`, `ASSEMBLY_CUT`, …}; {0, 1} | Assembly pure reads (`last_shape_change_T()` names the kind, MSA-33; `ragged_breach_open()` is true while a RAGGED cut's keep-side room is still venting (hull hole open, band not VACUUM) or a keep-side port is still uncapped within `RAGGED_WITHHOLD_MAX_TICKS`; registered, source Modular Ship Assembly) *(Amended 2026-10-28 — cross-GDD fix)* | The ruled withhold (D54): a RAGGED cut's `ASSEMBLY_CUT` is not due while the breach is open; `event_pending` stays latched and the event is taken once the read turns false, until the keep-side cut room has vented (Assembly's read, band VACUUM) and its keep-side ports are capped or the port ceiling has passed. `ASSEMBLY_WELD` and a SEALED cut (no stubs, so the read is false) are never withheld by their own entry. *(Amended 2026-10-27 — re-review)* While a RAGGED cut's entry is pending and the breach is open, **no entry of any kind** fires a capture, so a cut followed by a weld cannot capture inside the open breach (the weld entry waits with the cut); event order no longer matters |
536	| `AUTOSAVE_INTERVAL_TICKS` ★ | int | 5 400 … 18 000, default 10 800 *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review)* | Tuning Knobs | Interval trigger (3 min) |
537	| `AUTOSAVE_MIN_GAP_TICKS` ★ | int | 900 … 3 600, default 1 800 *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review)* | Tuning Knobs | Floor between any two `AUTO`/`EVENT` generations; strictly below the interval |
538	| `elapsed` | int | 0 … unbounded | calculated | Sim ticks since the last durable capture |
539	| `due`, `kind` | bool, enum | {0, 1}; {`AUTO`, `EVENT`} | calculated | Input to F-2; `kind` is stored in the header and `SaveInfo` (an event and the interval due on the same tick produce **one** save, kind `EVENT`) |
540	
541	**Output Range:** boolean `due` plus `kind`. `T < last_save_T` cannot occur after the reset-on-restore rule; if observed, `elapsed := 0`, `last_save_T := T` and `SL_AUTOSAVE_CLOCK_REGRESSION` is logged once. No interval save is ever due while the kernel is `PAUSED` (`T` cannot advance). The `QUIT` kind is a separate path (SL-6, F-2) and never passes through `due`.
542
